questions.q: What does the jab, jab, jab, right hook formula describe?
a: Giving value repeatedly before asking for a sale
Posting daily and deleting older content
Alternating paid ads with entertaining posts
Building a list and emailing it every week
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the phrase means give, give, give, and then ask.

questions.q: What should shape the content you post on each social platform?
a: The platform's own context and native style
One message reused across every network
The number of hashtags each site allows
The length of your competitors' most popular posts
questions.why: Lesson 2 says context matters more than content, so each post must fit its platform.

questions.q: What three qualities should your social media content have?
a: Not annoying, not too demanding, and native to the platform
Frequent, inexpensive, and highly promotional
Clever, controversial, and likely to go viral
Personal, poetic, and long enough to explain everything
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists these three tests for crafting content that works.

questions.q: Why does the summary say businesses must be on social media?
a: That is where people's attention has moved
It is cheaper than every other advertising channel
Search engines now ignore traditional websites
Customers expect discounts only available there
questions.why: Lesson 1 says marketers should go wherever the attention is.

questions.q: What makes Instagram especially attractive for engagement?
a: Its single feed and huge, broad user base
Its support for long-form written articles
Its strict chronological sorting of posts
Its focus on professional networking
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites its one-feed format, hundreds of millions of users and reach across ages.
